data.summary: The plan builds a solid foundation in Limits and Continuity first, then moves through differentiation, integration, and differential equations, ensuring each unit is introduced early and revisited before the exam. Weekly 5‑hour blocks combine focused topic study, targeted practice tasks, and live class participation when available, with the final weeks dedicated to mixed review and timed practice.

tasks: Read textbook sections for 1.1‑1.5 and take concise notes.
Do 12 limit‑evaluation problems (including graph and table estimates).
Check answers with solution guide and note any misconceptions.

weeks.focus: Consolidate limits and begin average rates of change
tasks: Attend live class 10800 and actively answer in‑class questions.
Complete 8 practice problems on average rate of change (2.1‑2.2).
Review class notes; redo any limit problems that were missed.
Watch a short video on derivative notation and power rule.
Do 10 derivative calculations using the power rule (2.5).
Practice estimating derivatives at points (2.3) with 6 graph problems.
Read section on chain rule; write summary of steps.
Solve 8 chain‑rule problems and 6 implicit differentiation problems.
Check work against answer key; correct any algebra errors.

weeks.focus: Inverse functions and related rates intro
tasks: Derive derivative formulas for inverse trig functions (3.4).
Complete 5 related‑rates starter problems (4.4).
Write a one‑paragraph explanation of how derivative gives meaning in context (4.1).

weeks.focus: Applications of differentiation – motion and rates
tasks: Solve 6 straight‑line motion problems (position, velocity, acceleration).
Do 5 non‑motion rate‑of‑change problems (4.3).
Create a quick‑reference sheet for motion formulas.

weeks.focus: Mean Value and Extreme Value Theorems
tasks: Read textbook sections on MVT and EVT; list hypotheses for each theorem.
Complete 8 problems applying MVT (5.1) and 8 identifying extrema and critical points (5.2).
Summarize differences between global and local extrema in a table.
Determine intervals of increase/decrease for 6 functions (5.3).
Apply the First Derivative Test to 6 functions (5.4).
Create a flowchart that shows steps from derivative to classification of extrema.
Compute left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums for 4 functions (6.2).
Translate a Riemann‑sum expression into sigma notation (6.3).
Write a short paragraph describing how accumulation relates to the integral.
Solve 8 problems that use the FTC to evaluate definite integrals.
Practice finding accumulation functions for 5 given rates.
Check each solution with calculator and note any sign errors.
Model 4 real‑world situations with differential equations (7.1).
Verify solutions for 4 DEs by differentiation (7.2).
Create a cheat‑sheet of common DE forms and their solutions.

weeks.focus: Slope fields and qualitative DE analysis
tasks: Sketch slope fields for 3 differential equations (7.3).
Interpret behavior of solutions from slope fields (7.4).
Write brief explanations of how initial conditions affect solution curves.

weeks.focus: Applications of integration – average value and motion
tasks: Compute average value of 5 functions on given intervals (8.1).
Use integrals to find position from velocity and vice‑versa for 4 scenarios (8.2).
Summarize key formulas on a one‑page sheet.

weeks.focus: Further integration applications – area and accumulation
tasks: Find area between curves for 5 pairs of functions (8.4).
Solve 4 applied problems using accumulation functions (8.3).
Review all integration techniques in a 10‑minute self‑quiz.

weeks.focus: Mixed review – core concepts and problem types
tasks: Do a 20‑question mixed‑topic practice set (one from each listed code).
Mark answers using the scoring guide; note any recurring errors.
Re‑watch brief video summaries for any topics with >2 mistakes.

weeks.focus: Timed full‑length practice and final review
tasks: Take a 90‑minute timed AP practice section covering all listed topics.
Score the section, compare to rubric, and write a one‑page reflection on weak areas.
Review error log and redo 5 of the most missed problems without notes.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, simulate exam conditions with a full timed section, then focus on fixing the specific mistakes you identified. Keep a calm mindset, review your quick‑reference sheets, and ensure you get plenty of rest before the January 19 exam.
